blocks.text: VALENCIA CITY, Bukidnon — Weather officials have clarified that the early morning haze blanketing parts of Bukidnon is caused by localized weather patterns and temperature drops rather than transboundary smoke from Indonesia. Weather specialist Christian Emmanuel of the Mindanao Regional Services Division of the Philippine Atmospherical, Geophysical and Astronomical Services Administration (Pagasa), told the Inquirer Saturday morning, September 19, that the fog consists of tiny water droplets formed by continuous early-morning temperature cooling. Residents, including morning walkers who observed landmarks like Musuan Peak (Mt. Kalayo), a boundary of Valencia City and Maramag town, enveloped in the mist, had initially suspected smoke […]...
